text:
The most likely corrupted element is **Mb2**, the PMOS diode that generates the `pb` bias. Its +20% sensitivity on slew (-21.1%) is the largest of any element, and it is the only one whose size change alone could plausibly close the roughly 21% slew shortfall (1.648e7 vs 2.1e7 V/s). A bias-generator fault like this is also consistent with the rest of the bias chain, where the mirror currents agree (Mb1, Mb2, and M0 all carry about 10 µA). M5 is second because its headroom is marginal and its slew sensitivity is nearly as large. M4 is third because its sensitivity is smaller and it shares the same `pb` bias. The sensitivities alone don't prove which element was changed, so this ranking is a best estimate.

```json
{"ranking": ["Mb2", "M5", "M4"], "fault": "Mb2 (pfet diode of the pb bias generator, W=1.396/L=0.3) is oversized. Its extra width lowers Vsg and pulls pb up, which reduces the M3/M4 PMOS source currents and starves the folded-cascode branches, so slew falls to about 16.5 V/us. Restoring Mb2 to its nominal width (roughly 20-25% smaller) should recover slew to the 21 V/us target."}
```
